clue.text: No other organisation can compete with it

definitions.text: No other organisation can compete with it

parts.words: No other organisation can compete with it
parts.note: describes a market held by one firm alone, so rivals are shut out entirely

explanation.definitionFit: A firm with exclusive control of a trade faces no competitors, which is the economic sense of the word.

clue.text: German city I take a Norwegian artist round

indicators.note: the painter's name is placed round the clue's I, enclosing it

parts.note: Edvard Munch, the Norwegian painter of The Scream

explanation.surface: A traveller describes carrying a painter's work around a Bavarian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts I inside MUNCH; 'take' and 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Bavaria is a major city in southern Germany.

clue.text: A struggle between northern and southern sea forces

indicators.note: the A and the struggle sit between the northern and southern letters

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

explanation.surface: A naval battle between fleets from north and south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' places A + VIE between N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleets of warships maintained by nations are their naval forces at sea.

clue.text: Worthless friend put to the test

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a companion who was put through a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trifling or of little value is meagre and worthless.

clue.text: Mislaid rosette and forfeited popularity?

definitions.meaning: a favour is a ribbon or rosette worn as a badge, here one that has gone missing
to fall out of someone's good graces

explanation.surface: Someone loses their prize ribbon and their public standing at once.
explanation.walkthrough: A favour is a rosette or knot of ribbon worn to show support, so the first reading is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings use the phrase: a missing ribbon badge, and the idiom for losing others' approval.

clue.text: A mistake schoolchildren bring back

indicators.note: bringing something back here means reading the word for schoolchildren backwards

parts.note: pupils are schoolchildren

explanation.surface: Children bring home an error from school.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder or error is a careless slip.

clue.text: Scottish bird confusing veal with a seaside confection

indicators.note: confusing the meat's letters muddles them into a new order

parts.note: rock is the hard sugar stick sold at British seaside resorts

explanation.surface: A strange recipe mixing veal with a sweet from the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' rearranges VEAL into LAVE. ROCK is the British seaside sweet, a hard sugar stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The skylark is called the laverock in Scots and northern dialect.

clue.text: Its place could well be at the foot of the column

definitions.text: Its place could well be at the foot of the column

parts.words: Its place could well be at the foot of the column
parts.note: read as a newspaper column the foot is the bottom of the text; architecturally it is the base supporting a pillar

explanation.definitionFit: A plinth or base on which a pillar or statue stands sits at the bottom of a column.

clue.text: Sort of step many debtors neglect to make

definitions.text: Sort of step many debtors neglect to make

parts.words: Sort of step many debtors neglect to make
parts.note: suggests a kind of footstep, but it is the sums owed that debtors fail to hand over

explanation.definitionFit: Debtors often fail to settle instalments of money owed, and these sums are what they must make.

clue.text: Writer isn't upset about unorthodox love

indicators.note: about means the first jumble goes round the second
upset letters are knocked over into a different arrangement
unorthodox means irregular, so this word's letters take a non-standard order

explanation.surface: Someone protests at an unconventional romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ISNT into NIST and 'unorthodox' turns LOVE into OVEL; 'about' wraps NIST round OVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An author of fiction books is a writer.

clue.text: Eagerly excited lady ringing a classical sextet

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the jumbled letters go round the sextet
excited means stirred up, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A thrilled woman phones a group of six classical musicians with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' makes ADLY from LADY; 'ringing' puts VI inside, after the A. 'Classical' points to Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with keen enthusiasm is doing it with avidity.

clue.text: What the helpful or unhelpful husband may do when the family meal is over

definitions.text: What the helpful or unhelpful husband may do when the family meal is over

parts.words: What the helpful or unhelpful husband may do when the family meal is over
parts.note: the helpful one removes the dishes from the table; the unhelpful one simply leaves

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to tidy away the plates and, as slang, to go away.

clue.text: The sea-wife swears it could be

indicators.note: it could be signals that the letters of the word could be rearranged into the answer

explanation.walkthrough: 'it could be' rearranges SWEARS. 'Sea-wife' is an old name for this fish, not a mermaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea-wife is a dialect name for a brightly coloured fish of the rocky shore.

clue.text: A defender who is prepared to shoot, if need be

definitions.text: A defender who is prepared to shoot, if need be

parts.words: A defender who is prepared to shoot, if need be
parts.note: a protector carrying a gun, ready to fire

explanation.definitionFit: A security escort carrying a firearm protects people or property and will fire if necessary.

clue.text: Where elephants bathe on the Gulf of Guinea?

definitions.text: Where elephants bathe on the Gulf of Guinea?

parts.words: Where elephants bathe on the Gulf of Guinea?
parts.note: elephant tusks give ivory, and a shore where they bathe is a coast; the country lies on that gulf

explanation.definitionFit: The West African nation Côte d'Ivoire lies on the Gulf of Guinea; the English name is a literal translation.

clue.text: Servant girl who might help with manicure?

definitions.text: Servant girl who might help with manicure?

parts.words: Servant girl who might help with manicure?
parts.note: a manicure treats the hands, so a maid for the hands

explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a female servant splits into a maid for the hands.

clue.text: Some brisk court play for high society, maybe

parts.note: a smart pace is a brisk one
a set is a unit of play in tennis on a court

explanation.surface: A lively game of tennis for fashionable people.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable socialites form an elite group in high society.

clue.text: Moving on to a different line?

definitions.text: Moving on to a different line?

parts.words: Moving on to a different line?
parts.note: sounds like changing a career or an argument, but means switching railway carriages between tracks

explanation.definitionFit: Railway carriages are pushed from one track to another in a siding.

clue.text: They provide poor accommodation

parts.note: suggests shoddy lodgings, but means housing for poor people

explanation.definitionFit: Charitable homes built for the elderly poor provide them with lodging.

clue.text: Horrified at having wild hags brought in

indicators.note: brought in means the jumbled letters are put inside the two letters of at
wild means out of control, so these letters run riot

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled at a gang of unruly old women entering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges HAGS into GHAS; 'brought in' places it inside AT. 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being struck with shock and dismay is being horrified.

clue.text: Rings up with material comfort

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading the letters bottom to top

parts.note: O's: rings are O shapes
lace is a delicate fabric

explanation.surface: Someone telephones and finds consolation in fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OS (rings as O's) into SO; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Consolation in grief or distress is comfort.

clue.text: The suit we turn up with when working out of doors?

definitions.text: The suit we turn up with when working out of doors?

parts.words: The suit we turn up with when working out of doors?
parts.note: a card suit doubles as garden tools that turn up the soil

explanation.definitionFit: A suit of playing cards shares its name with the digging tools used in gardens.

clue.text: Venturesome medico swallowing a gin cocktail

indicators.note: swallowing means the doctor's letters take in the a

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A bold doctor downs a gin-based drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' puts A inside DR; 'cocktail' rearranges GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bold and willing to take risks is being venturesome.

clue.text: Contemporary cross-section of society?

parts.note: contemporary means of the same years, so a slice of people all born around the same time

explanation.definitionFit: A demographic band of people of similar years is a section of society sharing an age.

clue.text: Is able somehow to get safely down to rock-bottom

definitions.text: to get safely down to rock-bottom

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A climber is capable of reaching the foot of a cliff without harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Descending a rock face by rope lets a climber reach the base safely.

clue.text: French authoress describing Arab dance of stately character

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round, so the author's name encloses the other word

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of a French novelist

explanation.surface: A French novelist writes about an Arab performing a dignified dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means drawing a line round, putting SAND round ARAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow, stately Spanish dance in triple time is a dance of dignified character.

clue.text: The latest type of infatuation?

parts.note: latest means the last stage of life, when one dotes: senile fondness

explanation.definitionFit: Feebleness of mind in old age arrives late in life and is linked to doting, foolish fondness.

clue.text: Her advancement over chauvinistic male journalists might be resisted

definitions.text: Her advancement over chauvinistic male journalists might be resisted

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could be rearranged to form the answer

explanation.surface: A woman's promotion over sexist reporters meets opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' rearranges RESISTED; the whole clue is the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: A female newspaper chief rising above male reporters could face opposition from them.
